{{Short description|German physicist}}
[[File:Schröder,Manfred 1993 Göttingen.jpg|thumb|Manfred Schroeder (1993)]]
'''Manfred Robert Schroeder''' (12 July 1926 &ndash; 28 December 2009) was a German physicist, most known for his contributions to [[acoustics]] and [[computer graphics]]. He wrote three books and published over 150 articles in his field.<ref>[https://ethw.org/Oral-History:Manfred_Schroeder Interview] from [[IEEE]] history archive.</ref>

Born in [[Ahlen]], he studied at the [[University of Göttingen]] (1947–52), earning a [[vordiplom]] in [[mathematics]] (1951) and [[Dr. rer. nat.]] (1954) in [[physics]]. His thesis showed how small regular cavities in concert halls cause unfortunate resonances.

He joined the technical staff at [[Bell Labs]] in [[New Jersey]] (1954–) researching speech and graphics, securing forty-five patents.  With [[Bishnu Atal]], he advanced and promoted [[linear predictive coding]] (LPC) during the late 1960s to 1970s and then developed [[code-excited linear prediction]] (CELP) in 1985. Still affiliated with Bell, he rejoined [[University of Göttingen]] as ''Universitätsprofessor Physik'' (1969) becoming [[professor emeritus]] (1991). 
<ref>[[Ning Xiang]] and [[Gerhard M. Sessler]]:{{cite book|title=Acoustics, Information, and Communication -- Memorial Volume in Honor of Manfred R. Schroeder, Springer 2014|doi=10.1007/978-3-319-05660-9|year = 2015|isbn = 978-3-319-05659-3|editor1-last=Xiang|editor1-first=Ning|editor2-first=Gerhard M|editor2-last=Sessler}}</ref> He was a visiting professor at [[University of Tokyo]] (1979).

With [[Ning Xiang]] he was a promoter of a synchronous dual channel measurement method using reciprocal maximum-length sequences (2003). He led a famed study of 22 concert halls worldwide, leading to a comparison method requiring no travel.

==Awards and honors==
*1969 First Prize at the International Computer Art Competition for his application of concepts from mathematics and physics to the creation of artistic works.
*fellow of the Acoustical Society of America
*[[IEEE Fellow]] (1971).<ref name="IEEE_Transactions_Bio">{{Cite journal | last1 = Schroeder | first1 = M. | title = Direct (nonrecursive) relations between cepstrum and predictor coefficients | doi = 10.1109/TASSP.1981.1163546 | journal = IEEE Transactions on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing | volume = 29 | issue = 2 | pages = 297–301 | year = 1981 }}</ref>
*[[Audio Engineering Society]] fellow and Gold medalist (1972)
*Member of the [[United States National Academy of Engineering]] (1979), for "founding the statistical theory of wave propagation in multi-mode media and contributions to speech coding and acoustics".<ref name="NAE">{{cite web|url=http://www.nae.edu/MembersSection/Directory20412/28600.aspx |title=NAE Members Directory – Dr. Manfred R. Schroeder |publisher=[[United States National Academy of Engineering]] |access-date=June 3, 2011}}</ref>
*Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (1986).<ref name=AAAS>{{cite web|title=Book of Members, 1780-2010: Chapter S|url=http://www.amacad.org/publications/BookofMembers/ChapterS.pdf|publisher=[[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]|access-date=June 3, 2011}}</ref>
*Helmholtz Medal of the German Acoustical Society
*1975 [[Max Planck Society]] appointed foreign scientific member
*[[New York Academy of Sciences]] member 1978
*[[Rayleigh Medal]] 1987<ref>{{cite web | last=Flanagan | first=James L. | title=MANFRED ROBERT SCHROEDER: 1926–2009 | website=National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine | date=2009-12-28 | url=https://www.nationalacademies.org/read/13160/chapter/59 | access-date=2025-11-27}}</ref>
*[[ASA Gold Medal|Gold Medal]] from the [[Acoustical Society of America]] (1991), for "theoretical and practical contributions to human communication through innovative application of mathematics to speech, hearing, and concert hall acoustics".<ref>{{cite web|title=Acoustical Society of America Awards, Gold Medal|url=https://acousticalsociety.org/acoustical-society-of-america-awards/|publisher=[[Acoustical Society of America]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Gold Medal Award – 1991, Manfred R. Schroeder|url=http://acousticalsociety.org/about/awards/gold/12_10_10_schroeder|publisher=[[Acoustical Society of America]]|access-date=June 3, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110722200112/http://acousticalsociety.org/about/awards/gold/12_10_10_schroeder|archive-date=July 22, 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* ''ISCA Medal for Scientific Achievement'' from the [[International Speech Communication Association]] (2004).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.isca-speech.org/iscaweb/index.php/honors/medals?id=14 |title=ISCA Medal for Scientific Achievement |publisher=International Speech Communication Association |access-date=July 27, 2023 |archive-date=July 27, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230727034306/https://www.isca-speech.org/iscaweb/index.php/honors/medals?id=14 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
